title: Mushroom Risotto
subtitle: Creamy Italian rice with chestnut mushrooms
excerpt: A classic Italian risotto made with chestnut mushrooms, thyme, and a generous amount of parmesan. Good risotto needs patience and attention at the hob; the rice is added ladle by ladle until each one is absorbed before the next goes in. The result is rich and creamy without any added cream.
sourceNotes: Based on the northern Italian risotto ai funghi tradition, adapted from standard home-cooking approaches found across multiple Italian regional cookbooks.

content.text: Keep the stock warm in a separate pan while you make the risotto. Adding cold stock slows the cooking and can make the rice uneven. In place of white wine, white wine vinegar diluted with a little water gives the right acidity.

items.prepNote: kept hot in a separate pan

content.text: Heat the olive oil and 30g of the butter in a large, wide saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, undisturbed at first, until golden. Season and set aside.
In the same pan, reduce the heat to medium. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the arborio rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until the grains look translucent at the edges.
Pour in the diluted white wine vinegar and stir until absorbed.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each ladle to be absorbed before adding the next. This will take about 18 to 20 minutes.
When the rice is just tender and the risotto flows like lava when you move the pan, remove from the heat.
Stir in the remaining 30g of butter and the parmesan. Fold in the cooked mushrooms. Rest for 2 minutes, then serve immediately.

items.cause: Too little stock added or overcooked
items.fix: Loosen with a splash of hot stock and stir off the heat.

items.symptom: Rice is still chalky in the middle
items.fix: Add more stock a ladle at a time and keep stirring.

items.cause: Pan too crowded or heat too low
items.fix: Fry mushrooms in batches over high heat.
